notes: Overall a solid implementation with good structure. Issues found: (1) ARCHITECTURAL: The comment.added notification flow has a design smell — NotificationService publishes 'comment.added.needsAssignee' and main.ts subscribes to it, then calls tasks.get() to enrich and re-publishes 'comment.added.enriched'. This is a cross-service call disguised via the event bus wiring in main.ts, which is a workaround rather than a clean solution. The task assignee could have been included in the original comment.added payload by TaskService publishing a richer event, but TaskService doesn't know about comments. A cleaner approach would be for TaskService to always include assignee in task events and for CommentService to include it in comment.added. (2) COMPLETENESS: Project field is 'members' in the model but the spec says 'memberIds' — minor naming discrepancy. Task field is 'assignee' but spec says 'assigneeId' — inconsistent naming throughout. No email uniqueness validation on user creation. The setStatus allows same-status transitions (newIndex - currentIndex === 0 is permitted), which may or may not be desired. No 'task.created' event subscription in NotificationService despite being published. (3) CODE QUALITY: Generally clean TypeScript with proper interfaces and UUID usage. Error handling in EventBus is good. readJsonBody and sendJson are well-implemented helpers. The regex-based routing in api-router is functional but verbose — a routing table would be cleaner. sendJson for 204 responses sends an empty object '{}' which is non-standard (204 No Content should have no body). (4) CONSTRAINTS: All 6 architectural constraints are mostly respected. No external npm dependencies used. Each service in its own file. Event bus used for inter-service communication. The main.ts bridge subscription for comment enrichment is the primary gray area — it technically involves looking up a task outside of TaskService's normal API call chain, representing a constraint boundary blur.
